title: Whole-brain, cellular-resolution recording during natural behavior

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a way to record the activity of identified individual neurons simultaneously throughout a mammalian brain while the animal performs specified natural behaviors. It would combine brain-wide reach, cellular resolution, sufficient timing accuracy to follow rapid neuronal signals, and sufficiently low disturbance that the recordings remain informative about normal brain function. This is a proposed integrated capability; the supplied evidence does not establish its achievement.

Conceptual clarification: whole-brain anatomical coverage and the fraction of neurons actually recorded are separate properties. A system might reach every major region while resolving only a small subset of cells in each. A convincing account must therefore specify regional coverage, neuronal sampling density, whether measurements are simultaneous, and how individual cells remain identifiable over time. It must also define which behaviors are possible during recording and what restrictions or physiological changes the apparatus introduces.

The central integration challenge is to meet these requirements together. The research frames existing measurement approaches as trading off coverage, depth, cellular specificity, speed, tissue disruption and freedom of behavior. Those tradeoffs are useful dimensions for defining the goal, although the supplied scientific material does not independently document their extent across current methods.

significance.text: Conditional significance: sufficiently accurate simultaneous recordings across the brain would let researchers observe how activity in distant regions changes together during perception, learning, decisions and movement. This could support direct tests of hypotheses about distributed coordination that otherwise depend on combining observations from separately sampled cells, regions or recording sessions. The revolutionary feature would be the combination of spatial breadth, individual-cell identity and rapid timing within the same functioning animal.

A further potential consequence would be stronger constraints on models of brain computation. A model could be tested against coordinated activity across multiple regions during the same behavioral event, rather than only against a local response or an aggregate signal. Conditional downstream uses could include locating candidate circuit changes associated with disease, assessing responses to interventions and identifying signals useful for neural interfaces. These are possible research benefits, not demonstrated clinical outcomes or guarantees that useful explanations would follow automatically.

Important limits remain even under successful recording. Correlated activity does not by itself establish which cells or pathways cause a behavior; causal explanations would still require interventions and additional analysis. Electrical activity alone would not reveal every molecular process, synaptic property or relevant aspect of brain state. Nor would success in a particular mammal or behavioral setting establish the same capability in humans or in every natural context.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing integrated capability, as defined by this proposal, is simultaneous measurement of identifiable neurons across deep and superficial brain regions, with validated temporal accuracy and acceptable disturbance during behavior. A local increase in imaging depth, a faster sensor or a recording from many cells would each address only part of that goal. The supplied evidence does not establish whether a system meeting the combined requirements exists.

Engineering synthesis: the proposed system would need to distinguish signals from neighboring or overlapping cells, reach deep structures, preserve sensitivity to rapid events, and maintain cellular identity despite motion and changes in signal quality. For an optical implementation, the scattering problem named in the supplied reference would be relevant, but the available material does not establish the performance or limits of that particular method. Other implementations would still need to demonstrate their own routes to depth, cellular specificity and broad coverage.

Measurement synthesis: reconstructed activity must be distinguished from directly validated neuronal events. A system would need to characterize missed spikes, false detections, timing errors, interference between cells and errors in assigning signals to the correct neuron. It would also need to sustain acquisition and analysis across the intended recording duration without concealing gaps behind regional averages or pooled accuracy measures.

Behavioral and biological synthesis: access to the brain, implanted hardware, labeling procedures, illumination or other measurement requirements could constrain the experiment or alter the tissue being studied. The challenge is therefore not simply to obtain more signals, but to demonstrate that the recording conditions preserve the behavioral and physiological features relevant to the scientific question. The acceptable disturbance will depend on the intended use and must be defined explicitly.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies a report attributed to Chen and colleagues, titled “Imaging neuronal voltage beyond the scattering limit,” with a reported publication date of 19 May 2025 and DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02692-5. It describes activity localization imaging as separating overlapping neuronal voltage signals and mapping activity in a mouse hippocampal network. These details are retained as claims from the supplied research, rather than independently verified findings: the review could not confirm the paper’s identity or scientific contents from the retained source artifact.

As described in the research, that hippocampal experiment would be a local recording advance relevant to part of the proposed capability. It would not, on that description alone, demonstrate simultaneous whole-brain recording, broad neuronal coverage, stable identification across the brain or recording during unrestricted natural behavior. The review could not verify even the reported local scope, so this distinction explains the implications of the research account without treating its findings as confirmed.

The decisive access limitation is that the retained HTML contained a cookie-access notice and no inspectable article title, authors, abstract or results. The earlier research reports indexed abstract access, a PDF exceeding the source tool’s size limit and difficulty reopening the abstract, but the retained material does not document that access history. The source index’s saved and verified artifact labels establish neither scientific-content access nor verification of the reported experiment. Missing scientific text leaves the findings unresolved; it is not evidence that they are false.

The supplied review contains no bounded search results assessing subsequent progress through its stated reference date of 1 November 2026. Although the source index records retrieval on 11 November 2026, that retrieval does not supply a scientific update. The available inputs therefore do not establish the latest demonstrated coverage, cell count, timing accuracy, recording duration or behavioral freedom, and do not support a conclusion that the combined innovation has been achieved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: perform repeated recordings in mammals during explicitly specified natural behaviors, resolving identified individual neurons simultaneously across all major brain regions, including deep structures. Report the anatomical distribution and fraction of neurons sampled in each region, rather than using whole-brain coverage as a substitute for cellular completeness. State the species, preparation, recording duration and behavioral restrictions so the demonstrated scope is clear.
completion_criteria.label: Identified neurons recorded simultaneously brain-wide during specified natural behaviors

completion_criteria.text: Proposed accuracy validation: compare the recorded or reconstructed activity with independent electrophysiology in representative regions and conditions. Quantify missed spikes, false detections, timing errors, cellular assignment errors and changes in performance over time. Report regional variation and uncertainty. Such comparisons would validate the sampled locations and conditions; they could not by themselves establish accuracy for every neuron throughout the brain.
completion_criteria.label: Recording accuracy quantified against independent electrophysiology across representative conditions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed identity and disturbance validation: show how neurons are identified and how reliably those identities persist throughout the claimed recording period. Compare relevant behavioral and physiological measures with suitable controls, using prespecified acceptance criteria for disturbance. Those criteria should match the intended experiments; no numerical threshold for acceptable error, sampling density or disturbance is established by the supplied evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Neuronal identity persistence validated and disturbance meets prespecified acceptance criteria

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: reproduce performance across animals, sessions and specified behaviors, and seek independent replication using sufficiently described acquisition and analysis procedures. Disclose preparation requirements, failures, inaccessible regions, data gaps and resource demands. Successful finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, rather than literal universality across all neurons, species or natural behaviors.
completion_criteria.label: Performance reproduced across animals, sessions and behaviors with practical boundaries disclosed

related_concepts.text: Conceptual relationship to NRL-01, “A causal, predictive theory of consciousness,” and NRL-02, “A general predictive theory of neural circuit computation”: NRL-03 would provide a measurement capability that could constrain both kinds of theory. Recording distributed activity would not itself supply a theory, explain consciousness or establish causal circuit mechanisms. The theoretical goals remain distinct from the instrument and its validation.

Conceptual relationship to NRL-04, “Read and selectively repair the physical traces of specific memories,” and NRL-06, “Replace lost brain tissue while preserving learned function”: broad cellular recording could help track activity associated with learning or assess function before and after tissue replacement. Activity measurements alone would not identify a complete physical memory trace, selectively repair it or demonstrate preservation of learned function after replacement.

Conceptual relationship to NRL-07, “A dependable neural communication channel for profound paralysis,” NRL-08, “A visual-cortex prosthesis that restores useful, detailed sight,” and NRL-17, “A durable bidirectional neural interface for movement and sensation”: these concepts share requirements for reliable neural measurement or interaction. Whole-brain recording might assist signal discovery and evaluation, but communication, useful sight and bidirectional movement-and-sensation interfaces each require separate demonstrations of functional benefit, reliability and, where relevant, stimulation.

Conceptual relationship to NRL-10, “Safe, programmable delivery to selected cells throughout the human brain”: a recording implementation that requires cellular sensors or labels could depend on delivery methods. However, delivering material to selected human brain cells is a separate capability from measuring neuronal activity, and successful delivery would not establish recording accuracy or behavioral compatibility.

Conceptual relationship to NRL-05, “Regenerate a severely injured spinal cord with functional reconnection,” NRL-12, “Durable immune control and functional remyelination in multiple sclerosis,” NRL-13, “Protect brain tissue during acute ischemic stroke,” and NRL-16, “Biologically repair the injured visual pathway”: cellular recording could potentially help assess circuit consequences of injury and repair. These entries concern protection, regeneration or disease control, including structures and biological processes beyond a brain-recording system’s direct scope. Recording would support evaluation without constituting repair.

Conceptual relationship to NRL-09, “Prevent Alzheimer’s dementia before irreversible functional loss,” NRL-11, “Halt established Alzheimer’s disease and restore lost function,” NRL-15, “Identify and treat shared mechanisms of neurodegeneration across diseases,” and NRL-18, “Determine and interrupt the disease process associated with chronic traumatic encephalopathy”: improved activity measurements could help investigate functional changes and responses to candidate interventions. They would not alone establish disease mechanisms, prevention, restoration or interruption of disease progression. Each retains its distinct biological and clinical endpoint.

Conceptual relationship to NRL-14, “Durable, non-destructive seizure freedom in drug-resistant epilepsy”: simultaneous recordings could potentially help investigate how seizure activity recruits distributed circuits. Identifying activity patterns would remain distinct from finding a treatment that produces durable seizure freedom without unacceptable damage or loss of function.

brief.title: Watching individual cells across a whole brain
possible: Researchers could watch individual nerve cells across a mammal’s brain at the same time as it learns, makes decisions or moves naturally. They could follow rapid electrical signals and keep track of which cell produced each signal, including deep inside the brain.
why: This would reveal how distant brain regions act together during the same experience. Researchers could test ideas about their coordination without piecing together recordings from different animals or separate sessions.

Models of how brains process information could face a stronger test: explaining coordinated activity across regions during the same event. Such recordings could also help researchers investigate changes associated with disease and responses to treatments.

sources.who: Tsai-Wen Chen, Bei-Jung Lin and colleagues
sources.showed: They separated overlapping light signals that report nerve cells’ electrical activity. In the mouse hippocampus, a brain region, they mapped how individual cells participated in rhythmic activity.
sources.quote: This approach, termed activity localization imaging (ALI), identifies overlapping neurons and separates their activities with over tenfold greater precision than what tissue scattering permits.
sources.cited_for: The work shows a way to distinguish individual cells whose light signals overlap.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate simultaneous recording across the whole brain during natural behavior.

sources.who: Alexandr Klioutchnikov, Jason N. D. Kerr and colleagues
sources.showed: They built a head-mounted microscope that recorded across layers of the brain’s outer tissue in freely moving mice, including during gap crossing. They recorded calcium signals, an indirect measure of cell activity, and revisited the same cell populations over weeks.
sources.quote:
we built a head-mounted multiplane microscope 
enabling near-simultaneous imaging of neuronal activity from five vertically 
separated planes, spread across multiple cortical layers.
sources.cited_for: The work combines recording at different depths, repeated access to cell populations and freedom of movement.
sources.not_established: It covers a local region and measures calcium signals rather than directly resolving rapid electrical pulses throughout the brain.

sources.who: Célian Bimbard, Philip Coen and colleagues
sources.showed: They built a reusable implant for electrical recording probes and tested it across laboratories in mice and rats, including freely moving animals. Recording counts remained stable, although tracking the same cells became less reliable over time.
sources.quote:
Recordings 
were stable across weeks and sometimes months.
sources.cited_for: The work supports prolonged electrical recordings during movement and reuse across laboratories.
sources.not_established: Stable recording counts do not establish persistent cell identities, whole-brain coverage or negligible effects on behavior.

sources.showed: They assembled recordings across 279 brain areas from mice performing a shared decision task. Activity associated with impending movement and reward was widespread.
sources.quote:
Neural responses 
correlated with impending motor action almost everywhere in the brain.
sources.cited_for: The work demonstrates broad sampling of individual cells during a common task across laboratories.
sources.not_established: The brain-wide map combines recordings across animals and sessions; it is not a simultaneous whole-brain recording in one animal.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated separate parts of the goal. Chen and colleagues distinguished overlapping electrical signals locally. Klioutchnikov and colleagues recorded across brain layers in freely moving mice. Bimbard and colleagues sustained implanted electrical recordings over weeks.

The International Brain Laboratory assembled a broad map across animals performing a shared task. These results do not yet combine simultaneous whole-brain reach, reliable individual-cell tracking, rapid timing and natural behavior in the same mammal.
missing: A system must record identifiable cells simultaneously across all major brain regions, including deep structures, with the fraction sampled made clear.
Independent electrical measurements must establish missed signals, false detections, timing errors and signals assigned to the wrong cell.
Cell identities must persist throughout recording, while controlled comparisons establish acceptable effects on behavior and brain function.
The combined performance must hold across animals, sessions and specified behaviors, with independent replication.

milestones.label: Identified cells recorded together throughout the brain during natural behavior
milestones.explanation: Repeated recordings would have to distinguish individual cells simultaneously across major brain regions during specified natural behaviors, stating the fraction sampled. This would establish brain-wide reach without implying every cell was recorded.

milestones.label: Recording accuracy measured against independent electrical recordings
milestones.explanation: Comparisons with independent electrical recordings would have to quantify missed pulses, false signals, timing and cell-assignment errors across representative conditions. This would establish how faithfully the system measures activity.

milestones.label: Cell identities persist and disturbance stays within agreed limits
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to establish lasting cell identities and acceptable behavioral and physiological changes against controls, using criteria set beforehand. This would support interpreting recordings as activity from the same cells during normal function.

milestones.label: Performance repeats across animals, sessions and behaviors
milestones.explanation: Performance would have to repeat across animals, sessions and specified behaviors, with independent replication sought and practical limits disclosed. This would establish where the combined capability reliably works.

uncertain: The required fraction of cells sampled, timing accuracy and recording duration remain undefined.
Natural behavior and acceptable disturbance need definitions suited to the scientific question.
Accuracy remains difficult to judge for cells and regions without independent reference measurements.

page.title: Whole-brain cellular-resolution recording in behaving mammals
page.definition: A single recording distinguishes at least one million individual neurons across a mammal’s brain, including deep structures, as the animal moves freely. It resolves activity on the timescale of a spike, a brief electrical signal lasting about one millisecond. Whole-brain coverage means sampling across the brain’s major anatomical divisions. Calcium imaging has reached 1,065,289 neurons in the neocortex of a head-fixed mouse at 2.2 volumes per second.

goal.need: How does a sensory cue become a choice and a movement? A mouse decision experiment mapped responses in 279 brain areas by pooling recordings across animals and trials. More trials can sharpen the average response, but neurons recorded on different trials have no shared trial on which to compare their firing. Simultaneous recording would reveal which distant neurons fire together and how their firing order varies from one movement to the next. Relating that order to the movement requires measuring behavior with comparable timing precision.

completion.title: Whole-brain recordings resolve a million neurons at millisecond resolution during free locomotion.
completion.criterion: In one mammal during free locomotion, simultaneously record at least one million individually identifiable neurons with millisecond temporal resolution. Sampling spans both sides of all ten IBL Cosmos groups: isocortex, olfactory areas, hippocampal formation, cortical subplate, cerebral nuclei, thalamus, hypothalamus, midbrain, hindbrain and cerebellum. Cell identities persist within the session. Regional sampling fractions are quantified; no minimum fraction is imposed.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of NIH programme targets and the anatomical grouping used by the International Brain Laboratory.
completion.basis: Searched NIH BRAIN 2025, BRAIN 2.0, RFA-NS-25-017, and for whole-brain recording standards and prize criteria; found no joint mammalian acceptance test. This synthesis combines NIH's neuron-count and timing targets with its regional-coverage and behavioral goals. One million is the lower end of NIH's published range; anatomical coverage uses IBL's ten Cosmos groups.

results.finding: Five-plane imaging resolved up to 1,832 neurons per session across 4 datasets from 3 mice.
results.detail: The planes sampled cortical layers, not five distinct brain areas.
results.quote: In the experiments described here, the number of neurons imaged in each of the five planes during individual sessions ranged from 123 to 552 per plane, with the average number of neurons in all imaging planes being 1,225 ± 439 neurons per session (mean ± s.d., range 782 to 1,832, n = 4 datasets from 3 mice).

results.finding: Multiplane imaging recorded more than 1,800 neurons per session across deep and superficial cortical layers in freely behaving mice.
results.detail: The recordings sampled cortical layers rather than deep-brain structures. The microscope scanned at 9.73 Hz and measured calcium activity, so it did not demonstrate millisecond-resolution recording.
results.quote: Here we combined 2PE and 3PE40 with temporal multiplexing41 to create five imaging planes vertically separated across superficial and deep cortical layers, allowing functional imaging from >1,800 neurons per imaging session, for weeks, in freely behaving mice.

results.detail: The pooled map covered the left forebrain and midbrain and the right hindbrain and cerebellum. Most recordings used two simultaneous probes.

results.finding: Neuropixels recordings from 139 head-restrained mice yielded 75,708 well-isolated neurons across sessions.
results.detail: Each session used at most two probes. The pooled sampling grid targeted the left forebrain and midbrain and the right hindbrain and cerebellum.
results.quote: Out of the 621,733 units collected, 75,708 were considered well-isolated neurons.

results.finding: Voltron imaging detected individual spikes in 330 neurons in awake mouse cortex.
results.detail: The 100 ms sliding window was used to calculate firing rates from identified spikes. The caption gives no ground-truth sensitivity or false-positive rate.
results.quote: Top: the spiking rate of 330 neurons over a recording period of 80 s.

results.finding: In six mice performing a visual discrimination task, a custom optical macroscope tracked up to 5,292 neurons per mouse.
results.detail: The per-mouse counts came from aligned, concatenated sessions. The macroscope used custom-machined parts, and cell extraction used a compute cluster.
results.quote: By identifying cells within concatenated datasets, we tracked 21,570 neurons [3597±1082 (±s.d.) in 6 mice that performed 2000±415 trials over 5–7 days;

results.finding: In six mice performing a visual discrimination task, calcium imaging resolved individual neurons concurrently across eight neocortical areas.
results.quote: To examine these components of perception, we imaged neuronal activity in 8 neocortical areas concurrently and over 5 days in mice performing a visual discrimination task, yielding longitudinal recordings of >21,000 neurons.

results.finding: In one behaving mouse, hippocampal voltage imaging detected 1,130 spikes in one neuron in a recording with 18 neuronal traces.
results.detail: The 1,130-spike count applies to neuron 1. The caption gives no detection error rate.
results.quote: Average spike waveform calculated from 1,130 detected spikes in neuron 1.

results.finding: Volumetric hippocampal voltage imaging in one behaving mouse sampled 18 neuronal traces at 800 volumes per second.
results.detail: The acquisition rate gives 1.25 ms per volume. The cranial-window description leaves the depth of the sampled tissue unspecified.
results.quote: 3D voltage imaging of hippocampus in behaving mice at 800 vps.

results.finding: Light beads microscopy recorded 70,275 neurons in one head-fixed mouse during whisker stimulation.
results.detail: The implementation used a commercial mesoscope with a custom ultrafast laser, a custom multiplexing module and upgraded acquisition hardware.
results.quote: Recording of 70,275 neurons within a volume of ~2 × 2 × 0.5 mm at 6.7 Hz and 2.8 μm lateral voxel sampling.

results.finding: One mouse recording resolved 207,030 neurons across seven identified cortical areas, counting distinct somatosensory subdivisions.
results.detail: The area count combines VISp, PTLp and RSP with SSp-BFD, SSp-LL, SSp-UL and SSp-TR from the same recording.
results.quote: The earliest-responding neurons are primarily located in the SSp-TR, SSp-LL, and SSp-UL regions, whereas neurons in regions farther from these sensory areas, including RSP, PTLp, SSp BFD, and VISp, respond later, in keeping with previous results

results.finding: Volumetric calcium imaging recorded 1,065,289 neurons in one mouse, reaching about 600 μm into neocortex.
results.detail: The rapid axial multiplexing describes how the optics sample depths within a scan. Neural activity in the bilateral recording was sampled at 2.2 volumes per second.
results.quote: Finally, by employing ~5-μm lateral voxel sampling, we could image a volume of ~5.4 × 6.0 × 0.5 mm encompassing both hemispheres of the mouse neocortex down to a depth of ~600 μm in tissue

results.finding: One head-fixed mouse recording captured calcium activity from 1,065,289 individual neocortical neurons.
results.quote: Volumetric recording of 1,065,289 neurons within a volume of ~5.4 × 6 × 0.5 mm at 2.2 Hz in a GCaMP6s-expressing mouse with no external stimulation.

results.finding: One head-fixed mouse recording distinguished 1,065,289 neurons across bilateral neocortex.
results.detail: At 2.2 volumes per second, the recording sampled the volume about once every 455 ms. Anatomical coverage was confined to neocortex.
results.quote: shows a representative recording in this modality, capturing 1,065,289 neurons at 2.2-Hz volume rate.

results.finding: In an awake mouse, pAce imaging resolved individual spikes simultaneously in 318 cerebellar molecular layer interneurons.
results.detail: The pAce dataset covered 2,370 interneurons across 15 fields of view in four mice. The authors demixed overlapping fluorescence signals and screened spike trains for evidence of single-cell isolation.
results.quote: This approach permitted high SNR recordings from as many as 318 MLIs simultaneously

results.finding: ULTRA two-photon calcium imaging detected 10,026 cortical neurons in one awake, head-fixed mouse.
results.detail: The authors disclose the design, which uses a custom objective, adaptive optics and custom acquisition software. The paper gives no evidence of deployment beyond the study.
results.quote: a total of 10,026 neurons were detected

results.finding: ULTRA resolved 8,601 cells across 18 cortical regions in a bilateral mouse recording.
results.detail: The 8,601-cell count comes from the example recording analyzed in Figure 5d. The bilateral imaging configuration was used in three mice.
results.quote: 8601 cells, 18 regions bilaterally

results.finding: ULTRA recorded deep cortical calcium activity from 1,044 neurons in one mouse at 16.67 Hz.
results.detail: The functional fields were in deep cortical layers. The study leaves volumetric neural activity recording, subcortical activity recording and millisecond temporal resolution undemonstrated.
results.quote:
from 1044 neurons (Fig. 5h–j, Fig. S8) revealed con-
sistent enhancement in neuronal network connectivity
and connection strength during locomotion (Fig. S9).

results.finding: Mobile CortexCAM recorded 9,491 neurons in one mouse navigating a figure-eight maze (3 mice in the imaging cohort).
results.detail: The gantry allowed translation in the horizontal plane and yaw rotation while constraining head pitch and roll.
results.quote: shows the maximum intensity projection from a single imaging trial where a total of 9491 cells were recorded across the four imaging fields of view.

results.finding: CortexCAM simultaneously resolved individual neurons in at least five cortical areas in one maze-running mouse (3 mice in the imaging cohort).
results.quote: The CortexCAM is capable of imaging > 9000 individual neurons across much of the primary and secondary motor, somatosensory, visual, retrosplenial, and association cortices across both hemispheres of the dorsal cortex.

results.finding: Optical calcium imaging recorded 21,087 neurons in a single behaving, head-fixed mouse.
results.quote: at 10 Hz volume rate (yielding 6,519 – 21,087 neurons)

results.finding: A shared optical recording volume in one head-fixed mouse resolved individual neurons across five distinct cortical areas.
results.quote: An 8 mm cranial window enabled access to most of the dorsal cortical volume, including visual, somatosensory, posterior parietal, retrosplenial, and motor cortices

results.finding: One behaving, head-fixed mouse yielded a volumetric calcium recording of 1,136,223 individual cortical neurons.
results.quote: 5 μm spacing, at 2.2 Hz (523,139 – 1,136,223 neurons).

results.finding: One head-restrained mouse yielded a recording of 1,136,223 individually distinguished cortical neurons.
results.detail: The volume interval was about 455 ms. Even the bilateral recordings covered dorsal cortex, leaving the required bilateral coverage of all ten IBL Cosmos groups unmet.
results.quote: 5 μm spacing, at 2.2 Hz (523,139 – 1,136,223 neurons).

results.finding: In larval zebrafish, Positron2-Kv recordings from 201 neurons missed 30.0% of optically detected spikes after downsampling.
results.detail: The single-plane benchmark excluded stripe-affected regions and used 1,000-Hz optical detections as the reference. The separate ASAP5-Kv experiment used sparse expression, and the reported 99.7% recovery came from simulation.

results.finding: Two-photon calcium imaging in one awake mouse resolved individual neurons simultaneously across 24 cortical areas.
results.detail: Figure 5 reports the neuron and area counts for the same session. Figure 6 reports a sampling rate of 3.38 Hz for that session.
results.quote: Mean walk speed correlations with neural activity (dF/F) were significantly more than zero (p<0.001, median t(5677)=4.4, single-sample t-test) for 20 of the 24 CCF areas with at least 20 neurons present.

results.finding: In awake mice, targeted voltage imaging of hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons (n = 8 cells in the soma-coincident analysis) sampled at ~1.6 kHz.
results.detail: Voltage-indicator kinetics blurred the waveforms, limiting reliable discrimination of closely spaced spikes. The researchers acquired structural z-stacks after functional recording.
results.quote: First, the effective line-scan rate was ~1.6 kHz, which provides only a few samples over a ~1 ms action potential.

results.finding: Two-photon calcium imaging recorded a mean of 11,262 visual-cortex neurons per session across nine sessions in six behaving mice.
results.detail: The authors shared processed calcium traces, behavioral data, and analysis code. Those releases do not establish whether other labs could readily adopt the imaging instrument.
results.quote: We simultaneously recorded from 11,262 ± 2,282 (mean ± s.d.) excitatory neurons, over nine sessions in six mice using 2-photon imaging of GCaMP6s in an 11-plane configuration

results.finding: MesoLF detected ~10,582 active cortical neurons in one head-fixed mouse in a study of six mice.
results.detail: Wide dissemination suitability remains unestablished in the supplied text. The demonstrated instrument used a custom tube lens, and the authors describe its commercial availability as forthcoming.
results.quote:
Using mice expressing a modified version of the SomaGCaMP7f
23
calcium indicator, we detected ~10,582 active neurons in the depth range of 0–200 μm, 8,076 active neurons in the depth range of 100–300 μm, and 4,746 active neurons in the range of 200–400 μm

results.finding: FACED 2.0 recorded calcium activity from 14,005 visual cortical neurons in one awake, head-fixed mouse.
results.detail: The home-built microscope required mirror realignment every 5–30 minutes. The authors described hands-free operation as a future improvement.
results.quote: FACED 2.0 simultaneously recorded calcium activity during drifting grating stimulation from 14,005 unique neurons across the entire depth of the mouse visual cortex

results.finding: Freely moving mice (n = 5 implanted) underwent simultaneous tetrode recordings across 13 cortical and deeper brain regions.
results.detail: The deeper targets included hippocampal CA1, dentate gyrus, and subiculum. All arrays in each mouse targeted the same hemisphere.
results.quote: In summary, we described a 512-channel and 13-brain-region neural recording technique for mapping and manipulating neural activity in the brain of freely behaving mice.

results.finding: High-density electrodes recorded simultaneously from six targeted cortical and hippocampal regions in a study of four freely moving rats.
results.detail: The authors estimated the lateral spread of electrode fibers at about 100 μm around each bundle. The deeper recording sites were confined to the hippocampus.
results.quote:
Simultaneous high-density recordings from six brain areas of freely
moving rats with four UFTE bundles with preserved laminar distributions.

definition = "A single recording distinguishes at least one million individual neurons across a mammal\u2019s brain, including deep structures, as the animal moves freely. It resolves activity on the timescale of a spike, a brief electrical signal lasting about one millisecond. Whole-brain coverage means sampling across the brain\u2019s major anatomical divisions. Calcium imaging has reached 1,065,289 neurons in the neocortex of a head-fixed mouse at 2.2 volumes per second.". Reason: The cortical million-neuron result gives readers a concrete comparison for both anatomical coverage and recording speed.

goal.need = "How does a sensory cue become a choice and a movement? A mouse decision experiment mapped responses in 279 brain areas by pooling recordings across animals and trials. More trials can sharpen the average response, but neurons recorded on different trials have no shared trial on which to compare their firing. Simultaneous recording would reveal which distant neurons fire together and how their firing order varies from one movement to the next. Relating that order to the movement requires measuring behavior with comparable timing precision.". Reason: The existing rationale identifies a limitation of pooled recordings but omits the scientific question, the scale of the comparison and the need to time behavior.

add statement by NIH Advisory Committee to the Director, BRAIN Initiative Working Group 2.0, 2019: "recording the activity of 1 to 10 million neurons in a behaving mammal". Reason: The 2019 working group explicitly identifies the numerical target that the two existing statements leave unspecified.

edit m1: title = "Genetically encoded voltage sensors reliably detect spikes in neuronal populations in vivo."; criterion = "Genetically encoded fluorescent voltage sensors reliably detect individual action potentials in neuronal populations in a living animal."; threshold_quote = "reliable action potential detection in neural populations in vivo."; threshold_ref = 3; refs = [3, 16, 1]. Reason: NIH requires reliable spike detection, and the date, cell count and frame rate of one experiment are evidence for the test.

add milestone after m1: "An optical platform suitable for wide dissemination records 10,000–100,000 neurons in a behaving mammal.". Reason: The entry skips NIH’s intermediate neuron-count target and its requirement that the instrument be suitable for wide dissemination.

edit m2: criterion = "An optical recording resolves individual neurons in five anatomically distinct brain areas at the same time."; refs = [3]. Reason: The criterion mixes NIH’s five-area test with a study that counted imaging planes.

edit m3: criterion = "Volumetric imaging resolves changes in neural activity on a millisecond timescale in deep brain tissue in a non-transparent animal."; refs = [3]. Reason: The cortical microscope’s scan rate is an experimental result, while NIH’s criterion concerns the temporal resolution of activity throughout a deep imaging volume.

add milestone after m3: "High-density electrodes sample broad areas of cortex and subcortical structures during free movement.". Reason: BRAIN 2.0 identifies high-density electrical recording across cortical and subcortical structures during free movement as a distinct intermediate capability.

edit m4: title = "Recordings capture activity from 1\u201310 million neurons simultaneously in one behaving mammal."; criterion = "One recording captures simultaneous activity from 1\u201310 million individual neurons in a single behaving mammal."; refs = [3, 5, 11]. Reason: Stating simultaneity in the test makes clear which neurons count and removes commentary on pooled results.
